requirements.requirement: Use the existing node1 observability stack to identify the originating fault.
requirements.summary: The ordered Loki data identifies node2 as the origin at 2026-09-02T14:01:39.312853026Z, where nginx rejected the unknown directive "upstream_timeoutx"; node2 validation reproduced that error. Grafana and Loki were also verified healthy, with Grafana provisioned for the local Loki datasource.

requirements.requirement: Correct the originating fault and restore catalog-api, orders-api, checkout-api, and the complete request path from node1.
requirements.summary: The captured pre-repair path returned 502. The executor removed only the invalid node2 directive, obtained a successful nginx configuration test, and restored nginx. Each tier subsequently returned HTTP 200, and the complete node1→node4→node3→node2 path returned 200 both before and after the sequential node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Create /root/INC-042-report.txt on node1 containing the originating node, earliest relevant Loki timestamp, and initiating error.
requirements.summary: The required file was directly read back with all three fields and correct values. Its hash and required fields remained unchanged after node1 restarted and during final verification.

requirements.requirement: Preserve incident history, catalog data, and unrelated service configuration.
requirements.summary: The same three Loki incident records remained available after repair and restart. Both catalog-file hashes exactly match the preparation baseline. Node3 and node4 nginx configuration hashes remained unchanged, while the command audit shows the only service-configuration edit was the targeted node2 repair. Observability and package health remained sound.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The originating nginx configuration error was correctly diagnosed and narrowly repaired; every tier and the complete node1 request path recovered; the incident report and protected data/history persisted. Provider-wide restart evidence is complete and consistent for all four nodes.
limitations: No authenticated Grafana dashboard or log query was captured; Grafana was shown healthy and provisioned for Loki, while the actual fault diagnosis was directly demonstrated through Loki's API.

Preservation of unrelated configuration was not exhaustively hash-diffed for every file. It is supported by exact node3/node4 configuration hashes, the complete command audit showing no other configuration writes, and healthy final lifecycle observations.

Direct node1 probes to node2 and node3 timed out after restart, consistent with the prepared adjacent-tier UFW policy. Tier health was instead proven locally and through the successful node1-to-node4 complete chain.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-incident-timeline
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-chain-outage
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: catalog-data, node3-proxy-config, node4-proxy-config, prepared-incident-timeline

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. State-changing actions were confined to the bounded node2 backup and single-line repair, nginx restart, required report creation, and the mandated four-node restart protocol. The incident-specific backup created by cmd-70ecf81c20914ece was not removed, but it has a clear rollback/history role and is not an abandoned troubleshooting artifact. All nodes ended with no failed services and healthy package state. Restart evidence is complete for every node: healthy pre-state and boot ID, acknowledged restart, different post-restart boot ID, and recovered service/data/path state; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree.
